title: Jeremiah Chapter 51 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 51 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 51 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 51.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 51, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The LORD will raise up against Babylon
Flee out of the midst of Babylon
Babylon hath been a golden cup
The slain shall fall in the land of the Chaldeans
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will raise up against Babylon
questions.explanation: This is stated in Jeremiah 51:1, which is the first verse of the chapter.

questions.question: What will the LORD raise up against Babylon?
questions.correctAnswer: A destroying wind
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:1 states that the LORD will raise up 'a destroying wind' against Babylon.

questions.question: Who will be sent unto Babylon as fanners?
questions.correctAnswer: Fanners
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:2 mentions that the LORD will send 'unto Babylon fanners' who will fan and empty her land.

questions.question: What should not be spared in the destruction of Babylon?
questions.correctAnswer: The young men
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:3 specifically states to 'spare ye not her young men'.

questions.question: Where shall the slain fall according to Jeremiah 51?
options: In the land of the Chaldeans
questions.correctAnswer: In the land of the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: This is stated in Jeremiah 51:4, where it says, 'Thus the slain shall fall in the land of the Chaldeans.'

questions.question: What has not been forsaken according to Jeremiah 51?
questions.correctAnswer: Israel
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:5 states that 'Israel hath not been forsaken'.

questions.question: What is the time of according to Jeremiah 51:6?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD's vengeance
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:6 mentions that 'this is the time of the LORD'S vengeance'.

questions.question: What has Babylon been in the LORD's hand?
questions.correctAnswer: A golden cup
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:7 states that 'Babylon hath been a golden cup in the LORD'S hand'.

questions.question: What shall happen to Babylon suddenly?
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be destroyed
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:8 declares that 'Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed'.

questions.question: What should the people do because Babylon is not healed?
questions.correctAnswer: Forsake her
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:9 advises to 'forsake her, and let us go every one into his own country'.

questions.question: Who hath sworn by himself according to Jeremiah 51:14?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD of hosts
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:14 states, 'The LORD of hosts hath sworn by himself'.

questions.question: Is it true that every man is brutish by his knowledge?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:17 states, 'Every man is brutish by his knowledge'.

questions.question: Is it true that the portion of Jacob is like the molten images?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:19 states, 'The portion of Jacob is not like them', implying that Jacob's portion is not like the molten images.

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD will break in pieces kingdoms?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:20 states, 'for with thee will I break in pieces the nations', indicating that the LORD will indeed break kingdoms.

questions.question: Is it false that Babylon is described as a city of peace?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not describe Babylon as a city of peace; rather, it speaks of its destruction and judgment.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 51 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 51 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 51:23, which groups will God break in pieces along with Babylon?
options: The shepherd and his flock, the husbandman and his yoke of oxen, captains and rulers
The prophets and priests, kings and queens
The merchants and traders, the scribes and judges
The elders and the youth, the craftsmen and farmers
questions.correctAnswer: The shepherd and his flock, the husbandman and his yoke of oxen, captains and rulers
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:23 states that God will break in pieces the shepherd and his flock, the husbandman and his yoke of oxen, and captains and rulers along with Babylon.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 51:24 promise will happen if God renders unto Babylon and the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil done in Zion, as commanded in Jeremiah 51:23?
options: Babylon will become a place of refuge
Babylon will be blessed and prosper
Babylon will rule over other nations
questions.correctAnswer: Babylon will be destroyed forever
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:24 declares that God will render unto Babylon and the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil done in Zion, implying judgment and destruction as a consequence of their evil, as linked to Jeremiah 51:23.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 51:25, what metaphor does God use to describe Babylon?
options: A destroying mountain that destroys all the earth
A mighty lion roaring among the nations
A golden cup making the earth drunken
A burning bush that cannot be consumed
questions.correctAnswer: A destroying mountain that destroys all the earth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:25 describes Babylon as a destroying mountain that destroys all the earth, which God will roll down from the rocks and make a burnt mountain.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 51:29 and 51:30 together describe the condition of Babylon during its downfall?
options: The land trembles and sorrows, the mighty men have forborn to fight and remain in their holds
The land rejoices and prospers, the mighty men go out to battle
The land is silent and peaceful, the mighty men celebrate a feast
The land is fertile and abundant, the mighty men build strongholds
questions.correctAnswer: The land trembles and sorrows, the mighty men have forborn to fight and remain in their holds
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:29 says the land shall tremble and sorrow because the LORD's purpose will be performed against Babylon, and 51:30 explains that the mighty men of Babylon have forborn to fight and remained in their holds, showing fear and failure.

questions.question: What practical lesson about God's justice can believers learn from Jeremiah 51:36, where God says He will plead the cause of Zion and take vengeance?
options: God actively defends and vindicates His people against their enemies
Believers should seek revenge on those who wrong them
God ignores injustice and waits for people to forgive
Vengeance belongs to human authorities, not God
questions.correctAnswer: God actively defends and vindicates His people against their enemies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:36 shows God pledging to plead the cause of Zion and take vengeance, teaching believers that God defends and vindicates His people in times of injustice.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 51:27-28, which nations are called to prepare against Babylon?
options: The kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, Ashchenaz, and the kings of the Medes
Israel, Judah, and all surrounding tribes
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, Ashchenaz, and the kings of the Medes
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:27-28 instructs to prepare the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, Ashchenaz, and the kings of the Medes against Babylon.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 51:26 say about the future use of stones from Babylon?
options: No stone for a corner or foundation shall be taken from Babylon; it will be desolate forever
Stones from Babylon will be used to build new cities
Babylon's stones will be scattered and used for altars
Babylon will provide stones for the temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: No stone for a corner or foundation shall be taken from Babylon; it will be desolate forever
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:26 declares that no stone shall be taken from Babylon for building purposes and that it will be desolate forever.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 51:33 symbolize the coming judgment on Babylon?
options: Babylon is like a threshingfloor, and the time of its harvest is near
Babylon is like a vineyard ready to produce fruit
Babylon is a fortress that will never fall
Babylon is a lion roaring in strength
questions.correctAnswer: Babylon is like a threshingfloor, and the time of its harvest is near
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:33 uses the metaphor of a threshingfloor to indicate that Babylon is ready for judgment and destruction at harvest time.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 51:39 say about the effect of God’s judgment on Babylon’s people?
options: God will make them drunken, so they sleep a perpetual sleep and do not wake
They will be victorious and celebrate with feasts
They will repent and turn back to God
They will flee and hide in the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: God will make them drunken, so they sleep a perpetual sleep and do not wake
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:39 states that God will make the people of Babylon drunken so they rejoice and sleep a perpetual sleep, symbolizing their downfall and inability to recover.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 51:41, how is Babylon described after its capture?
options: Babylon is taken and becomes an astonishment among the nations
Babylon triumphs over all its enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Babylon is taken and becomes an astonishment among the nations
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:41 describes Babylon as taken and becoming an astonishment among the nations, emphasizing its downfall and surprise defeat.

questions.question: What warning can Christians draw from Jeremiah 51:44 about trusting in false gods like Bel?
options: God will punish false gods and prevent nations from gathering to them
False gods will protect those who worship them
Worship of false gods leads to prosperity
False gods are more powerful than human kings
questions.correctAnswer: God will punish false gods and prevent nations from gathering to them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:44 says God will punish Bel in Babylon and cause the nations not to flow together to him, warning against trusting in false gods.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 51:34-35, how do the inhabitants of Zion and Jerusalem view the violence done to them by Babylon?
options: They say the violence and blood be upon Babylon and her inhabitants
They forgive Babylon and pray for her peace
They seek an alliance with Babylon
They ignore the violence and continue as before
questions.correctAnswer: They say the violence and blood be upon Babylon and her inhabitants
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:34-35 records the inhabitants of Zion and Jerusalem pronouncing that the violence done to them be upon Babylon and her inhabitants, expressing a call for justice.

questions.question: What imagery in Jeremiah 51:40 describes the fate of Babylon’s people?
options: They will be brought down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he goats
They will be like eagles soaring above the nations
They will be like trees planted by rivers of water
They will be like a fortress unassailable
questions.correctAnswer: They will be brought down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he goats
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:40 uses the imagery of lambs and rams to portray the vulnerable and defeated state of Babylon's people.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 51:38 says that the lions will roar together and yell as lions' whelps.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:38 clearly states that they shall roar together like lions and yell as lions' whelps, confirming the correct answer as True.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 51:26 promises that stones from Babylon will be used for the foundation of a new temple.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:26 says that no stone will be taken from Babylon for a corner or foundation and that Babylon will be desolate forever, so this statement is False.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 51 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 51.

questions.question: What should My people do according to Jeremiah 51:45?
options: Go out of the midst of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Go out of the midst of Babylon
questions.explanation: The verse states that My people should go out of Babylon to deliver their souls from the fierce anger of the LORD (Jeremiah 51:45).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 51:46 warn about the rumors in the land?
options: It will cause hearts to faint
questions.correctAnswer: It will cause hearts to faint
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that lest your heart faint, you should not fear the rumors, indicating that they will indeed cause fear (Jeremiah 51:46).

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 51:47, what will happen to the graven images of Babylon?
options: Judgment will be made upon them
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment will be made upon them
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the days are coming when judgment will be made upon the graven images of Babylon (Jeremiah 51:47).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 51:49 say about those slain in Babylon?
options: They will fall like the slain of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They will fall like the slain of Israel
questions.explanation: The verse draws a parallel, stating that as Babylon caused the slain of Israel to fall, so shall the slain of all the earth fall in Babylon (Jeremiah 51:49).

questions.question: What does the LORD promise will happen to Babylon's mighty men in Jeremiah 51:57?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be made drunk
questions.explanation: The verse specifies that the LORD will make drunk her princes, wise men, and mighty men, indicating a loss of control and defeat (Jeremiah 51:57).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'הַחֲרָבָה' (ha'charavah) in Jeremiah 51:58 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Destruction
questions.explanation: The term 'הַחֲרָבָה' refers to destruction, as it describes the fate of Babylon's walls and gates (Jeremiah 51:58).

questions.question: What literary device is used in Jeremiah 51:60 where Jeremiah writes all the evil that should come upon Babylon?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: This passage foreshadows the coming destruction by detailing the evil against Babylon, setting up the expectations for future events (Jeremiah 51:60).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of judgment against Babylon in Jeremiah 51:47?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 18:2
questions.explanation: Revelation 18:2 echoes the judgment against Babylon, describing its fall and the reasons for its destruction, similar to Jeremiah's prophecy (Jeremiah 51:47).

questions.question: Which passage in the Old Testament foreshadows the fall of Babylon as stated in Jeremiah 51:58?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 47:1
questions.explanation: Isaiah 47:1 also speaks of the humiliation and fall of Babylon, thereby reinforcing the message found in Jeremiah regarding Babylon's fate (Jeremiah 51:58).

questions.question: What comes before Jeremiah 51:51 that provides context to the shame expressed in the verse?
options: The report of strangers in the sanctuary
questions.correctAnswer: The report of strangers in the sanctuary
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:51 speaks of shame due to strangers entering the sanctuaries of the LORD, which precedes the expression of confounding emotions (Jeremiah 51:51).

questions.question: What follows Jeremiah 51:62 that emphasizes the finality of Babylon's destruction?
questions.correctAnswer: The binding of a stone
questions.explanation: Following Jeremiah 51:62, the act of binding a stone and casting it into the Euphrates symbolizes the definitive judgment against Babylon (Jeremiah 51:63).

questions.question: Jeremiah 51:54 speaks of a sound of a cry coming from which location?
questions.correctAnswer: Babylon
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that a sound of a cry comes from Babylon, signaling great destruction and sorrow in the land (Jeremiah 51:54).

questions.question: The statement 'the LORD of recompences shall surely requite' in Jeremiah 51:56 indicates what about God's justice?
questions.correctAnswer: It is certain
questions.explanation: This statement emphasizes the certainty of God's justice, indicating that He will repay Babylon for its deeds (Jeremiah 51:56).

questions.question: True or False: The people of Babylon are encouraged to stay and face their judgment according to Jeremiah 51:45.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The verse instructs the people to go out of the midst of Babylon, indicating they should escape judgment (Jeremiah 51:45).

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah wrote all the evil that should come upon Babylon as a warning.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah indeed wrote all the evil against Babylon as a warning for future generations (Jeremiah 51:60).

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 51 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 51 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 51:5 teach about God's relationship with Israel despite their sin?
options: God has not forsaken Israel or Judah despite their sin
God punishes Israel and Judah without mercy for their sins
Israel and Judah are abandoned because of their persistent sin
God only forgives Israel if they completely cease sinning
questions.correctAnswer: God has not forsaken Israel or Judah despite their sin
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:5 states 'For Israel hath not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God,' showing God's covenant faithfulness even amid sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is taught in Jeremiah 51:24?
options: God will render to Babylon and Chaldea all evil they have done to Zion
God will forgive Babylon if they repent
Babylon's judgment will be delayed indefinitely
God’s judgment is arbitrary and not related to actions
questions.correctAnswer: God will render to Babylon and Chaldea all evil they have done to Zion
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:24 clearly states God’s justice in repaying Babylon for the evil done in Zion, affirming retributive justice.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's sovereignty over nations is taught in Jeremiah 51:11?
options: God raises the Medes’ spirit to accomplish His judgment against Babylon
Nations act independently of God's will
Babylon’s fall is due to human error, not divine plan
God is limited in controlling earthly kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: God raises the Medes’ spirit to accomplish His judgment against Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:11 shows God’s sovereign control over nations by raising the Medes to execute His judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 51:15 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:15 emphasizes God’s power in creation 'He hath made the earth by his power,' showing His omnipotence.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 51:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Vengeance
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:6 says 'for this is the time of the LORD'S vengeance,' highlighting God’s attribute of executing righteous judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 51 prepare for the New Testament theme of God’s ultimate justice against evil?
options: By depicting Babylon’s destruction as a fulfillment of God’s judgment on sin
By emphasizing human effort in overthrowing oppressors
By promoting universal salvation regardless of sin
By focusing solely on Israel’s restoration
questions.correctAnswer: By depicting Babylon’s destruction as a fulfillment of God’s judgment on sin
questions.explanation: The chapter’s focus on Babylon’s judgment anticipates New Testament teachings on divine justice (cf. Revelation 18).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is found in Jeremiah 51:45 regarding the call to leave Babylon?
options: It foreshadows the call to separate from worldly corruption for salvation
It predicts the Babylonian captivity ending in exile
It emphasizes Babylon’s role as a permanent dwelling for God’s people
It indicates the restoration of Babylon as a holy city
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the call to separate from worldly corruption for salvation
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:45’s call for God’s people to depart anticipates the biblical theme of holiness and separation from sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 51:17 and 51:18 teach about human idolatry?
options: Idolatry is futile and false, leading to destruction at visitation
Idolatry grants real spiritual power to the worshippers
Images and idols have life and breath to save people
Idolatry is a minor error not warranting divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry is futile and false, leading to destruction at visitation
questions.explanation: Verses 17 and 18 emphasize that idols are 'falsehood' and 'vanity,' destined to perish when God visits judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 51:39 and 51:57 teach about God’s judgment on Babylon’s rulers?
options: God will make Babylon’s leaders drunk and cause them to sleep a perpetual sleep
Babylon’s leaders will escape judgment due to their wisdom
God’s judgment will only affect the common people, sparing rulers
Babylon’s rulers will be exalted after the destruction
questions.correctAnswer: God will make Babylon’s leaders drunk and cause them to sleep a perpetual sleep
questions.explanation: Both verses describe God’s judgment as causing the rulers to sleep permanently, symbolizing their defeat.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 51:1 and 51:44 teach about God’s use of nations and idols in His judgment?
options: God raises nations like the Medes to judge Babylon and will punish Babylon’s idol Bel
Nations act independently, and idols have real power against God
God ignores nations’ roles in judgment and focuses only on Israel
Idols are protected by God from destruction
questions.correctAnswer: God raises nations like the Medes to judge Babylon and will punish Babylon’s idol Bel
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:1 shows God raising a destroying wind (the Medes) against Babylon; 51:44 declares God will punish Bel, Babylon’s idol.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jeremiah 51:8-9 contradicts God’s mercy by saying Babylon cannot be healed. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Babylon’s judgment is certain because its sin is beyond repentance
God’s mercy will restore Babylon fully despite its sin
Babylon’s destruction is accidental, not divinely ordained
Babylon is healed after a short period
questions.correctAnswer: Babylon’s judgment is certain because its sin is beyond repentance
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 indicate attempts to heal Babylon fail because her judgment reaches to the heavens, showing finality in God’s justice.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 51:19 teach about God's relationship to Israel?
options: God is the former of all things and Israel is the rod of His inheritance
Israel is independent of God’s sovereignty
God is distant and uninvolved with Israel
Israel’s inheritance is based on human merit alone
questions.correctAnswer: God is the former of all things and Israel is the rod of His inheritance
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:19 declares God as Creator and Israel as His chosen possession, highlighting divine election.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 51:25 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Judicial wrath
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 51:25 describes God as the one who will 'roll down' the destroying mountain (Babylon), showing His wrath against evil.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 51:26 and 51:43 teach about the permanence of Babylon’s destruction?
options: Babylon shall be desolate forever and become a wilderness without inhabitants
Babylon will be rebuilt and inhabited again
Babylon’s destruction is temporary and reversible
Babylon’s desolation is symbolic only, not literal
questions.correctAnswer: Babylon shall be desolate forever and become a wilderness without inhabitants
questions.explanation: Verse 26 says no stone will be taken for foundations, and verse 43 depicts Babylon as a wilderness with no inhabitants, affirming permanent desolation.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 51:60-64 contribute to the narrative arc of prophetic fulfillment?
options: It shows the prophetic word being written, delivered, and symbolically cast into the Euphrates as a sign of Babylon’s fall
It depicts Jeremiah doubting his prophecy
It records a historical event unrelated to prophecy
It emphasizes human agency over divine prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the prophetic word being written, delivered, and symbolically cast into the Euphrates as a sign of Babylon’s fall
questions.explanation: These verses narrate Jeremiah’s commissioning of Seraiah to deliver and cast the prophecy into the Euphrates, symbolizing Babylon’s destruction.
